quotes.quote: Existing evaluation methods often adapt text-based benchmarks, overlooking speech's unique characteristics and challenges, including prosody, homophones, stuttering, and differing user expectations.
Here, we introduce the first comprehensive benchmark designed to systematically evaluate end-to-end speechLLMs in practical speech conversations.
We further design a query-aware evaluation method to use customized evaluation checklists and prompts to enhance the accuracy of automatic evaluation.
Table 1: Comparison between WildSpeech-Bench with other benchmarks.
WildSpeech-Bench deliberately focuses on establishing a robust foundation for single-turn evaluation, a critical but currently unmet need in the field.
We utilized the WildChat dataset (Zhao et al., 2024) as the query source to align the data with real-world conversational scenarios.
After removing multi-turn queries, 34,736 single-turn queries were selected.
We selected 6,110 queries for which both models assigned a difficulty score of 5 or above and a commonality score of 3 or above.
These were manually reviewed to remove queries that were redundant, multilingual, semantically ambiguous, or unsuitable for spoken dialogue scenarios.
The resulting high-frequency categories included: Information Inquiry (II), Solution Request (SR), Opinion Exchange (OE), and Text Creation (TC).
Due to an overrepresentation of Information Inquiry queries, we randomly removed a portion of them to achieve a balanced distribution across categories, yielding 1,000 retained queries.
resulting in 100 Paralinguistic-Featured (PF) queries
In summary, our dataset is composed of a total of 1,100 queries with five different major categories.

This response is then transcribed into text using Whisper-large-v3 (Radford et al., 2023).
Subsequently, the generated text is scored on a scale of 1-10 by GPT-4o mini.
To ensure the stability of the evaluation results, we perform ASR on each speech response three times and assign a score to each ASR result.
The final result is the average of the three scores.
Besides assessing the linguistic and semantic qualities of the model's speech output, we also evaluated its audio acoustic quality using UTMOS (Saeki et al., 2022).
Specifically, we crafted comprehensive and customized checklists for open-ended queries.

The final dataset comprises 1,100 queries, with 1,000 drawn from general speech interaction categories (Information Inquiry, Solution Request, Opinion Exchange, Text Creation) and 100 from the Paralinguistic-Featured category.
The curation process resulted in a focused dataset of 1,100 high-quality queries, emphasizing diagnostic depth over sheer volume.
